title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing and partial-JSON delimiter handling
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Fixes rare SSE streaming corruption where partial JSON tokens could be split across chunks resulting in client parse errors. Improves OpenAI-compat framing and ordering guarantees for function/tool-calling sequences. No breaking changes; behavioral fixes under existing API surface.
description: Context: clients (OpenAI-compat and native SSE) observed occasional JSON parse errors and mis-ordered token/event delivery when the server emitted large generation payloads that were chunked at network boundaries. Root causes included: 1) naive chunk flush that could split JSON strings/objects across SSE events; 2) missing explicit event delimiters between adjacent 'data:' blocks under high-throughput batching; 3) race between tokenization emitter and framing logic which allowed out-of-order 'event:' headers for function/tool-calling streams. Motivation: these failures cause downstream SDKs and customers to see partial JSON, invalid JSON arrays, or tool-calling sequences where the function name/arguments arrive after the finalizing token, breaking structured-output workflows.
commits: 3 commits: 1) canonicalize/sse: introduce streaming-buffer reassembler and token-boundary tracker; 2) sse/framing: ensure explicit "data:" delimiter emission and stable event ordering; 3) tests: add unit/e2e tests for partial-json and openai-compat regressions
high_level_changes: Add buffer_reassembler to coalesce TCP/chunk boundaries and track JSON depth to avoid splitting JSON tokens across events
Make frame_writer always emit explicit 'data: ' prefixes and an empty line delimiter between events
Serialize partial JSON in a compatibility-safe wrapper when we must emit an incomplete object, with a "partial":true flag for SDKs to optionally buffer
Fix ordering: ensure event headers (type/seq) are emitted deterministically from the framing thread after token emission finished for that logical message
Improve OpenAI-compat adapter to translate our partial-event wrapper into a compat-friendly sequence that OpenAI SDKs expect
tests: Unit: buffer_reassembler edge cases (split string, escaped characters, unicode boundaries)
Unit: frame_writer delimiter and ordering checks
Integration: e2e simulated chunk boundaries with both native and openai-compat clients
Load/canary: 1% production traffic for 48h with extra logging
Regression: added test case reproducer from SUP-4321
testing_notes: Initial CI run failed due to a race in tests referencing global tokio runtime; fixed by isolating async runtime per test. Flaky integration test repro merged into test harness and stabilized. Performed canary rollout to 1% traffic across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 before full merge. Observed zero parse-error regressions in canary and improved 95th-percentile end-to-end latency for streaming by ~6% under high batching scenarios.
review_comments: Liam Chen: Please add a regression test that reproduces the broken OpenAI-compat sequence we saw in SUP-4321.
Aisha Kapoor: Added tests under crates/openai-compat/tests and updated integration e2e to include the reproducer.
Marisol Vega: Can you confirm that the partial-event wrapper will not change existing SDK behavior unless they opt-in to handling 'partial' flags?

Aisha Kapoor: The wrapper is compatibility-first: we only emit it when we cannot reassemble a full JSON object within reasonable latency; openai-compat adapter converts it into the usual data chunks so existing SDKs see no behavioral change.
Evan Brooks: Nit: prefer deterministic seq numbering to be monotonic per-connection — saw a potential overflow with long-lived connections.
Aisha Kapoor: Added seq wrap guard and unit test to ensure monotonic behavior across 2^32+ events.
Liam Chen: Approving after the canary shows no regressions.
notes_for_ops: Backfill: none. Rollout plan: canary 1% (48h) -> 10% (24h) -> full. If parsing errors spike by >0.1% or increased 5xxs observed for streaming routes, rollback to previous main and notify runtime on-call. Logging keys: sse.frame_reassembler.err, sse.frame_writer.order_violation.
changelog_entry: Fix: SSE streaming framing and partial JSON handling to eliminate client-side parse errors and improve OpenAI-compat sequencing (Aisha Kapoor)

Backport to release/2026-02 branch if customers on stable flagged by SUP-4321 request it
size_estimate: small-medium (runtime+adapter changes, tests). Risk: low; touched high-throughput path so careful monitoring required.
